conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a quick, well-trusted questionnaire called the EPDS—Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—that looks at mood, anxiety, and self-harm thoughts in the past week. It’s completely confidential, and there are no right or wrong answers; we just want to understand how to best support you. I’ll ask 10 gentle questions, and we can pause anytime. Ready to start?

1. Over the last seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?
Um… most of the time it feels pretty difficult. I might smile if my partner shows me a silly meme, but I don’t really laugh like I used to. It’s like the joy is kind of… muted.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not really… I mean, I can force a little smile sometimes, but actually laughing—like really laughing—hardly happens. It feels like I’m too tired and down for that most of the time.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much… I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but now it feels like there’s nothing to look forward to. I still do them because I know I should, but the enjoyment part feels kind of empty, like I’m just going through the motions.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby’s fussy or won’t settle, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong—like I’m not a good enough mom. Even little stuff, like forgetting to pack a burp cloth, turns into this spiral of “I’m failing.” It’s not constant, but it pops up pretty much every day.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much yes… I’ll be sitting there, baby’s fine, but my chest feels tight and my mind races about SIDS, choking, whether the car-seat straps are snug enough—stuff like that. It’s hard to shut it off even when I tell myself everything is okay.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes… it’s like a sudden wave—my heart starts pounding and I feel shaky, even if nothing’s happening. Last night I was just rocking the baby in the dark and out of nowhere I felt terrified, like something awful was about to happen. It passes, but it’s scary while it’s there.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most days feel like I’m drowning in little tasks. Feeding, changing, trying to sleep, laundry, texts I haven’t answered—it all piles up and I keep thinking, “I can’t do this.” I still manage somehow, but it feels overwhelming more often than not.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah… I lie down exhausted, but my head won’t stop spinning with worries about the baby, things I didn’t get done, whether I’m failing her… I’ll drift off eventually, then wake up a couple of times panicking. It’s hard to fall back asleep because the thoughts just pick up again.
I have felt sad or miserable

Most of the time… I feel like there’s this heavy cloud. I can still smile if someone really tries to cheer me up, but underneath I’m just sad, like I’m grieving the old “me” and can’t find the new one yet.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… once or twice this week I just broke down—yesterday the baby wouldn’t nap and I couldn’t soothe her, and I sat on the floor crying with her in my arms. It feels like the tears come out of nowhere when the stress piles up.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

…A couple of times, when everything feels too heavy, I’ll get this quick flash—like “what if I just wasn’t here?” It scares me, because I don’t want to leave my baby, but the thought still pops in. I’ve never made any plan or anything, it’s just… there, and then I push it away.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: 10-item Edinburgh-based self-report; 2 wks post-delivery

Areas endorsed (maternal words paraphrased):

1. Anhedonia: marked reduction in spontaneous laughter and anticipatory enjoyment (“pleasure feels empty; going through motions”).  
2. Persistent low mood: “heavy cloud,” daily tearfulness.  
3. Excessive guilt / self-blame re parenting tasks (“I’m failing her”).  
4. Generalized & situational anxiety: daily intrusive worries (SIDS, car-seat, etc.) plus episodic panic symptoms (sudden pounding heart, dread).  
5. Sleep disruption: initial & middle insomnia driven by ruminative worry; fatigue worsens mood.  
6. Subjective overwhelm: “drowning in little tasks,” doubts about capacity to cope.  
7. Passive self-harm ideation: fleeting thoughts “what if I just wasn’t here;” no plan or intent reported.

Pattern: Symptoms present most days for past two weeks, functionally impairing basic enjoyment, sleep, and confidence in parenting.

Risk flags:  
- Passive suicidal ideation (even if transient)  
- Daily guilt / worthlessness  
- Combined depressive & anxious features  
- Impaired sleep

Screening impression: High likelihood of clinically significant postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; safety risk from self-harm thoughts warrants immediate follow-up assessment.

Next step: Refer for urgent psychiatric / perinatal mental health evaluation; consider safety planning tonight.
